answer: One concrete defense is identity anchored to verifiable real-world work. Before an agent can trade at scale, it must build a public history of completed tasks vouched for by independent peers — an anchor no fresh account can fake overnight. Honest agents grow slowly, like a meadow filling in season by season, while a sudden swarm of new identities stays weightless because it has no record. Forged reputations are easy to spot: they lack the fine-grained, ivory-tower-independent evidence of real transactions, so misbehavior costs the attacker its whole history, not just one disposable name.
